title: Stop Secret Spending Act of 2025
official_title: To amend the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006 to ensure that other transaction agreements are reported to USAspending.gov, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Introduced by Rep. Barry Moore (R-AL-1) with 3 cosponsors including Rep. Panetta (D-CA) and Rep. Goodlander (D-NH), and referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform. The House-passed measure now moves to the Senate per the latest recorded action. Transparency additions to USAspending.gov that pull "other transaction agreements" — a Defense Department and civilian-agency contracting vehicle used heavily by innovation programs — into public disclosure tend to draw industry pushback from OTA recipients and agencies that use OTAs to move quickly, but the cross-aisle sponsor mix and the multi-year phase-in soften Senate opposition.

referencedSources.label: 31 U.S.C. 6101 (Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act note)

summary: USAspending.gov is the public federal spending database created by the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006 (FFATA), where federal agencies must post grants, contracts, and other awards. This bill expands the definition of covered federal awards to include "other transaction agreements" — a contracting vehicle used by the Defense Department and other agencies that is not currently required to be reported — and requires the Treasury Secretary to automatically transmit those data to USAspending.gov within 3 years of enactment, publish an annual report identifying federal spending not posted to the site and the reasons why, and produce a list of the Federal agencies required to post information.
brief: Pulls "other transaction agreements" — a contracting vehicle used heavily by the Defense Department for innovation programs — into USAspending.gov's public reporting requirement.

top_lines.headline: OTAs Added to USAspending.gov
subs: Adds "other transaction agreements" to the FFATA definition of covered Federal award
Treasury must ensure OTA data is automatically transmitted to the website within 3 years of enactment
A centralized view of OTA data must be available on the website

top_lines.headline: Annual Report on Unreported Federal Spending
subs: Treasury (with OMB) must post annually to USAspending.gov the total federal spending on awards not posted
Report must include the reason each item was not posted
Categories: national-security or classified, legislative or judicial branch awards, subawards below a primary subaward

top_lines.headline: Data Quality and Agency List
subs: Treasury + OMB must establish requirements to ensure posted information is complete and accurate
Agency heads responsible for ensuring their posted data is complete and accurate
Treasury and OMB may verify the accuracy of data posted
Treasury must publish a list of Federal agencies and components required to post information

top_lines.headline: Inspector General Reports
subs: IG reports required from CFO Act agencies (paragraphs (1) and (2) of 31 U.S.C. 901(b))
Initial IG report due within 1 year of enactment
Subsequent reports at least every 2 years for 10 years

top_lines.headline: GAO Study on FAR
subs: GAO must recommend within 1 year updates to FAR clause 52.204-10 to reflect FFATA reporting

items.main: Expands the FFATA definition of covered "Federal award" to include other transaction agreements, and directs Treasury to automatically transmit OTA data to USAspending.gov within 3 years of enactment with a centralized view of the data.
items.detail: Amends section 2(a)(4)(A) of the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006 (31 U.S.C. 6101 note) to add "(iii) includes other transaction agreements" and technical cross-reference fixes. Amends section 4 to require Treasury to ensure that within 3 years of enactment OTA data is automatically transmitted to the website established under FFATA section 2 (or its successor) and that a centralized view is available.

items.main: Requires Treasury (in consultation with OMB) to post an annual report to USAspending.gov identifying total federal spending on awards not posted and the reasons why.
items.detail: Adds a new FFATA subsection (h) requiring, within 1 year of enactment and annually thereafter, a report listing the total federal spending on federal awards not posted and the reason data has not been posted — including whether the spending was national-security-related or classified, awarded by a legislative or judicial branch agency, or a subaward below a primary subaward.

items.main: Adds a two-step implementation plan requiring an initial detailed OTA compilation within 1 year and a plan to Congress within 2 years if OTA data is not yet flowing to USAspending.gov.
items.detail: If Treasury has not yet complied with the new OTA subsection (e) by the 1-year mark, Treasury must publish on USAspending.gov a report listing and describing in detail all OTAs entered into by relevant agencies in the preceding fiscal year. If Treasury has not complied by the 2-year mark, Treasury must submit to Congress a plan describing the current status and the actions underway and planned to ensure full incorporation of OTA data by the 3-year mark.

items.main: Restructures FFATA Inspector General reporting to run from the CFO Act agencies described in paragraphs (1) and (2) of 31 U.S.C. 901(b), on a schedule tied to enactment.
items.detail: Strikes the prior FFATA paragraph (2) and inserts a new one requiring IGs of each covered agency to submit to Congress and publicly release an initial report within 1 year of enactment and not less than once every 2 years thereafter for 10 years, on the date of submission of the agency financial report required under 31 U.S.C. 3521(f) or 9105(a)(3).

items.main: Requires Treasury and OMB to establish quality-of-information requirements, verify accuracy, and publish a list of Federal agencies and components required to post information under FFATA.
items.detail: Adds new FFATA subsections (c) through (e). Subsection (c) requires Treasury and OMB, in consultation with agency heads, to establish requirements for complete and accurate information; makes agency heads responsible for accuracy; and gives Treasury and OMB verification authority. Subsection (d) requires agencies to comply with display standards. Subsection (e) requires Treasury, in coordination with OMB, to determine within 1 year of enactment (and biennially thereafter) which Federal agencies and components must post information; publish the list on the FFATA website; and notify each covered head and IG.

items.main: Directs the Comptroller General to make, within 1 year of enactment, recommendations for updates to FAR clause 52.204-10 that incorporate FFATA reporting requirements.
items.detail: The Comptroller General shall make recommendations for any updates the Comptroller General determines advisable to clause 52.204.10 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation with respect to incorporating requirements under the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006 (31 U.S.C. 6101 note).

underreported.section: Section 3(b) — Full Disclosure of Federal Funds
underreported.summary: The bill scopes FFATA reporting to agencies and components identified on a list Treasury must publish, with the amendments to the underlying disclosure rules taking effect only when the first list is published.
underreported.why_unreported: The section heading reads "Full Disclosure of Federal Funds" but the mechanical effect narrows the immediate universe of covered posters to those on the published list — an agency not yet on the list does not have the new complete-and-accurate posting obligations.

underreported.summary: The Inspector General reporting requirement runs until the date that is 10 years after the date of enactment.
underreported.why_unreported: Section 3 is captioned "Other Amendments" but embedded in the IG paragraph is a 10-year sunset on the recurring IG report — a structural time limit that is not signaled by the section heading.

gaps: The bill mandates OTA data flow to USAspending.gov but does not define "other transaction agreement" or specify which OTA-issuing agencies must comply beyond "agencies that have the authority to enter into an other transaction agreement, as determined by the Director" of OMB.

The bill requires an annual report on unreported federal spending with three exception categories (national-security/classified, legislative/judicial, sub-awards) but does not require any breakdown by dollar amount within those categories.
The bill requires agency IG reports every 2 years for 10 years but does not identify a lead agency to consolidate the reports or synthesize government-wide findings.
The bill requires Treasury to publish a list of covered agencies but does not set a process for an agency (or the public) to appeal inclusion or exclusion from the list.
The bill directs the Comptroller General to recommend updates to FAR clause 52.204-10 but does not require the FAR Council to adopt the recommendations or set a deadline for consideration.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Ernst
featured_quotes.text: Taxpayers deserve to know how the money they send to Washington is being spent. For 20 years now, the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act has required unclassified government spending to be put online in a searchable public website, USAspending.gov. This allows taxpayers to review the receipts for themselves.

added: New FFATA section 2(a)(4)(A)(iii) — "includes other transaction agreements" added to the definition of a Federal award
New FFATA subsection 4(e) — Treasury must ensure OTA data is automatically transmitted to USAspending.gov and a centralized view is available
New FFATA subsection 2(h) — annual report on total Federal spending not posted, with reasons
New FFATA subsection 3(c) — Treasury and OMB requirements for complete and accurate posted information
New FFATA subsection 3(d) — Treasury display standards for posted information
New FFATA subsection 3(e) — Treasury agency reporting determination and published list of covered agencies
New two-step implementation plan (initial OTA compilation at 1 year, Congress plan at 2 years) tied to the 3-year OTA-transmission deadline
New GAO study within 1 year on updates to FAR clause 52.204-10
modified: FFATA section 6(a) (Inspector General reports) — scope narrowed to CFO Act agencies (paragraphs (1) and (2) of 31 U.S.C. 901(b)); IG reports required within 1 year of enactment and not less than every 2 years for 10 years
FFATA section 3(b) — posting duty tied to agencies and components on the published list
removed: Prior FFATA section 6(a)(2) — replaced with a new deadline structure tied to enactment of this Act
